articles.abstract: The reasoning capabilities and broad general knowledge of Large Language Models (LLMs) make them a natural choice for interpreting user requests and managing energy in smart home contexts. However, LLMs lack specific knowledge about individual homes and the ability to predict future energy consumption, limiting their effectiveness in energy optimization and management. This paper introduces HyLL, a hybrid framework that integrates Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks for energy consumption prediction with an LLM, such as GPT-4o, enhanced through in-context learning for real-time optimization and energy management. The LSTM models predict daily energy usage for ten household appliances using historical data and weather conditions, ensuring accuracy through iterative updates. The LLM utilizes 24-hour energy predictions to guide users in shifting their energy consumption to off-peak hours and reducing usage during peak demand periods. By combining predictive modeling with AI-driven decision-making, HyLL improves energy efficiency, alleviates grid stress, and reduces consumer costs, underscoring the critical role of AI in sustainable smart home energy management.

articles.abstract: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) is driving significant power demand and introducing challenges for the secure operation of power grids. As a result, data centers are increasingly expected to act as active grid participants with obligations to provide demand response capabilities. This has created a need for AI training jobs to adjust their power consumption dynamically based on specific energy requirements. Existing methods are ad hoc, relying heavily on profiling, lacking effective memory optimization and adaptability, and failing to track reference power efficiently. We present PowerMorph, a solution designed to optimize hardware resources and AI training processes to efficiently manage energy consumption during operations. PowerMorph predicts power usage and performance through lightweight selective profiling and interpolation. It makes progressively better decisions, adapts to changing conditions during runtime, and reduces cold starts by analyzing historical data. PowerMorph offers an effective and reliable tracking approach to power demand response curves, ensuring higher throughput while preserving training accuracy. Evaluations on multiple large language models (LLMs), various GPU types, and across varying reference power curves demonstrate that PowerMorph maintains a low tracking error of just 1.8%, achieves up to 197.9% higher throughput, and reduces cold starts by 82.5%, without compromising training accuracy.

articles.abstract: PPrediction-based dynamic multiobjective evolutionary algorithms (DMOEAs) often fail to fully exploit comprehensive historical information when solving dynamic multiobjective optimization problems (DMOPs). To alleviate this challenge, this paper proposes a DMOEA with a large language model (LLM)-enhanced accumulated learning prediction for addressing DMOPs. Specifically, a bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) network is trained online using approximated Paretooptimal solutions from all previously encountered environments, enabling it to effectively capture the problem’s dynamics and maintain a favorable trade-off between convergence and diversity. Moreover, as a novel contribution to this field, an LLM is used to refine the BiLSTM model by generating high-quality solutions as enhanced training data, thereby substantially reducing prediction error and enhancing robustness. Comprehensive empirical studies have been conducted on 14 commonly used benchmark DMOPs and a real-world problem, which demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed algorithm over five competitive DMOEAs.

articles.abstract: As Large Language Model (LLM)-based agents increasingly run complex multimodal tasks on resource-constrained edge devices, existing frameworks fall short. Built for the cloud, these systems focus on discrete tool selection but neglect resource-aware parameter configuration, making them poorly suited to edge environments. To address these issues, this paper proposes Resource-Adaptive Planning (RAP) for efficient LLM tool calling in resource-constrained edge computing. Specifically: 1) RAP uses a retrieval-augmented adaptive scheduler to distribute workloads between edge-based Small Language Models (SLMs) and cloud-based LLMs based on estimated task complexity under resource constraints. 2) A model-based control mechanism decouples task planning from parameter optimization with reinforcement learning and a learnable environment model that simulates file-state changes to optimize execution parameters and reduce resource consumption during planning. 3) Experimental results show that RAP significantly outperforms existing baselines, achieving a 63% task success rate while reducing inference latency and peak memory usage by up to 62% and 29%, respectively.

articles.abstract: Power drone inspections have become a crucial method for monitoring the status of transmission lines and substation equipment. However, in real-world scenarios, defect targets typically exhibit features such as small scale, weak texture, and complex backgrounds with strong interference. The traditional model struggles to meet the demand for rapid on-site closed-loop resolution. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an on-site defect identification method for drone inspection scenarios based on spatial reasoning learning from multimodal image-text large models. First, we develop a defect image generation method using Variational Autoencoders (VAE) and conditional score matching diffusion. By embedding semantic information into the feature layer of the U-Net decoder via the multi-layer Spatial Adaptive Normalization and Decomposition (SPADE) operator, we precisely control the generation location and morphology of defect features. Second, at the model level, a visual encoder based on Swin Transformer is constructed. A hierarchical window attention mechanism extracts multi-scale defect and scene topological features. A text encoder is built using the Next Token Prediction pre-training method and a large language model, combined with domain-specific fine-tuning using power system terminology databases and equipment ledger knowledge. At the cross-modal fusion layer, a contrastive learning mechanism aligns defect images and textual descriptions within a unified vector space. For spatial reasoning learning, we construct visually-linguistically intertwined regional inference samples. Region-level instruction fine-tuning drives the model to perform dynamic region cropping and multi-step reasoning analysis. Regarding on-site deployment, we combine CPU-NPU heterogeneous co-acceleration with memory optimization strategies. Through dynamic task allocation and data prefetching techniques, we achieve low-power, low-latency real-time edge inference. Experimental results demonstrate that our method delivers high-precision and high-efficiency defect detection in power inspection scenarios, effectively addressing complex backgrounds and resource-constrained field environments.
